newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to adopt floating oil-price system in July.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to adopt floating oil-price system in July.

text.p: Taiwan monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp will adopt a new floating price system on July 1 to fully reflect fluctuations in the international oil market, state media reported on Sunday.
Under the new system, domestic petroleum prices are expected to be reduced in July to respond Taiwan's falling crude import costs, state media said.
Starting from July 1, the state-owned company's petroleum prices would be adjusted every two weeks on the basis of import costs, rather than a few times a year as is currently done.
Chinese Petroleum's oil import costs averaged US$17.76 per barrel in May, higher than the $15.26 budgeted for the period but lower than April's $18.74, company figures show.
Chinese Petroleum has boosted local prices by about 12 percent in 1997, with an average nine percent increase on January 1 and a further 2.97 percent rise on April 4.
Executives have said the added revenues were needed, despite a general decline in world crude prices, to cover an accumulated budgetary deficit for the fiscal year ended June 30.
As of May, Chinese Petroleum had accumulated a deficit of T$15.196 billion from the current fiscal year.
